solution.what: The existing siena1421 collection survey records unsuccessful homophonic/null-aware attempts on nos. 20 and 23; this contribution does not rerun or claim those attempts.
Transcribed with CTTS, then solved by GPT-6 Astra, as confirmed by George Lasry. Shared key applied to nos. 20 and 23; subsequent image and editorial review retained uncertain passages.

Imported the current CTTS snapshot and latest edited lines; 4,254 cipher occurrences, 59 observed classes. Preserved CLEAR1-CLEAR4, tentative Sforza and Paolo Orsini, repeated Name6, and the unresolved Eucebio reading.

Used the supplied keys-and-sources report and independently checked Fermo’s April 1413 parallel, Minuti’s Sforza account, Meister pp. 51 and 55–57, and later Mazzone camp records. Spring 1413 and the identities remain proposed; 1421 belongs to another Siena piece. Comparable Lucca Sforza sign is post-recovery support, not the matched alphabet.

Only R4811 CTTS L6-L10 mechanically decoded: 322 signs yield 328 literal letters matching the normalized current edition, with no spelling emendation. Refreshed the visual key and English translations. Full editions remain editorial readings, not a full mechanical validation.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 322 tokens, 40 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.126 per letter; random keys -4.009 (z 7.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.749 (mean -2.785, z 21.8); annealer on the real text -2.443. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.126; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.443 Scope: deliberately selected R4811 L6-L10 only, not the full key or edited texts. 328 literal letters become 325 scored letters under the model normalization.
